data.body:
LANDED. Change 1739 merged as 50cc45f0d1 ("Hoist the sweep history walk out of the lock").

Verified against the MERGED tree rather than trusting the submit — all four parts are on main:
- `_sweep_position_map` returns None (not `{}`) on failure, so a failed build degrades to
  per-TICKET walks instead of the per-EVENT pathology;
- scoped staging (`git add -- <tid>/`) instead of `git add -A`;
- `_sweep_should_yield` re-probes the store lock between tickets;
- `_build_authorship_ledger` takes the optional prebuilt position map.

Effect: a store-wide sweep now performs ONE `git log` history walk, built before any lock is
taken, instead of one per ticket inside the store write lock. The deployed reality was worse
than the ticket description said: per-ticket map misses were falling through to per-EVENT
wildcard walks (the `'*<event-id>*.json'` pathspec the pony lane captured), and a leading
wildcard defeats pathspec pruning so each was a full-history scan.

Final local verification on the merged commit: main tier 12850 passed / 0 failed; integration
193 passed with one live-Jira index-visibility flake reproduced identically across two runs and
unrelated to compaction; ruff, mypy (527 files), complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0, and the
module-size contract all clean.

What this ticket cost, recorded because it is the useful part: the plan took three review
rounds and the code took three more, and the reviewer found real defects in all six. Two would
have been SILENT — a path-keyed map that would have missed every lookup and quietly restored
per-event walks, and an empty-dict fallback strictly worse than the bug being fixed, while my
own comment on that line asserted the opposite. My tests were vacuous three separate times: an
isinstance-only assertion, an unsigned fixture that made two ledger assertions compare empty
lists, and a theft test with no positive half. And twice an edit I believed had applied had
not, because `ruff format` had reflowed the target string — caught once by counting
replacements and once by mypy.

Follow-up filed and deliberately left open: `camerashy-erectable-frog` — a blocked writer sees
only a bare pid in `flock: could not acquire lock`, with nothing saying the holder is optional
housekeeping that is safe to interrupt. That guarantee already exists in `run_sweep`'s docstring
and never reaches the operator; it cost the pony lane 24 minutes and forced a manual kill.
